topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself and outlines the objectives of the lecture on cancer causes, environmental exposures, and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Biological Foundations and Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by mutations arising from endogenous cellular processes, replicative stress, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey diverse environmental carcinogens and examine epidemiological evidence showing how lifestyle, geography, and migration impact cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how pathogens such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites contribute to cancer, featuring Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical pathways through which specific dietary toxins, radiation, and xenobiotic compounds cause DNA damage and mutational changes.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, cellular promoters, and host developmental timing facilitate tumor development.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.
